title: KCET 2011 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: If $\dfrac{\log x}{b-c}=\dfrac{\log y}{c-a}=\dfrac{\log z}{a-b}$, then the value of $x^{b+c}\cdot y^{c+a}\cdot z^{a+b}$ is .................
questions.explanation: Let the common ratio be $k$, so $\log x=k(b-c)$ etc. Then $\log(x^{b+c}y^{c+a}z^{a+b})=k[(b+c)(b-c)+(c+a)(c-a)+(a+b)(a-b)]=k[(b^2-c^2)+(c^2-a^2)+(a^2-b^2)]=0$, so the value is $e^0=1$.
The $r$-th term is $\dfrac{\sum_{k=1}^r k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^r k}=\dfrac{2r+1}{3}$. Summing from $r=1$ to $n$ gives $\dfrac{n^2+2n}{3}=\dfrac{n(n+2)}{3}$.

questions.q: If $n$ is an odd positive integer and $(1+x+x^2+x^3)^n=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{3n} a_r x^r$, then $a_0-a_1+a_2-a_3+.........-a_{3n}$ is = .................
questions.explanation: Putting $x=-1$ gives the alternating sum $=(1-1+1-1)^n=0^n=0$ since $n\geq 1$.

questions.q: If $r^{th}$ and $(r+1)^{th}$ terms in the expansion of $(p+q)^n$ are equal, then $\dfrac{(n+1)q}{r(p+q)}$ is ..........
questions.explanation: $T_r=T_{r+1}$ gives $\binom{n}{r-1}p^{n-r+1}q^{r-1}=\binom{n}{r}p^{n-r}q^r$, which simplifies to $pr=q(n-r+1)$, i.e. $q(n+1)=r(p+q)$, so the ratio equals 1.

questions.q: If $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are roots of $x^3-2x+1=0$, then the value of $\displaystyle\sum\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha+\beta-\gamma}\right)$ is ...........
questions.explanation: $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0$ so $\alpha+\beta-\gamma=-2\gamma$. The sum becomes $-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha}+\dfrac{1}{\beta}+\dfrac{1}{\gamma}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha}{\alpha\beta\gamma}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{-2}{-1}=-1$.

questions.q: Define a relation $R$ on $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ as $xRy$ if $x$ divides $y$. $R$ is ............
questions.explanation: Every element divides itself (reflexive) and divisibility is transitive, but $1$ divides $2$ while $2$ does not divide $1$, so $R$ is not symmetric; hence reflexive and transitive only.

questions.q: The negation of $p\to(\sim p\vee q)$ is ...........
questions.explanation: $p\to(\sim p\vee q)\equiv \sim p\vee(\sim p\vee q)\equiv \sim p\vee q$, whose negation is $p\wedge\sim q$.

questions.q: In any triangle $ABC$, the simplified form of $\dfrac{\cos 2A}{a^2}-\dfrac{\cos 2B}{b^2}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Using $a=2R\sin A$, $\dfrac{\cos 2A}{a^2}=\dfrac{1-2\sin^2A}{4R^2\sin^2A}=\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}$; the $-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}$ terms cancel on subtraction, leaving $\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{b^2}$.

questions.q: Angles of elevation of the top of a tower from three points (collinear) $A$, $B$ and $C$ on a road leading to the foot of the tower are $30^0$, $45^0$ and $60^0$ respectively. The ratio of $AB$ to $BC$ is ............
questions.explanation: If the tower height is $h$, distances from the foot are $h\sqrt3, h, h/\sqrt3$ for $A,B,C$. So $AB=h(\sqrt3-1)$ and $BC=h(\sqrt3-1)/\sqrt3$, giving $AB:BC=\sqrt3:1$.

questions.q: The value of $\sin10\cdot\sin30\cdot\sin50\cdot\sin70$ is ............
questions.explanation: Using $\sin\theta\sin(60-\theta)\sin(60+\theta)=\dfrac14\sin3\theta$ with $\theta=10$: $\sin10\sin50\sin70=\dfrac14\sin30=\dfrac18$. Multiplying by $\sin30=\dfrac12$ gives $\dfrac{1}{16}$.

questions.q: Locus of a point which moves such that its distance from the $X$-axis is twice its distance from the line $x-y=0$ is ............
questions.explanation: $|y|=2\cdot\dfrac{|x-y|}{\sqrt2}$. Squaring, $y^2=2(x-y)^2$, which simplifies to $2x^2-4xy+y^2=0$.
Slope of $AB=\dfrac{4-2}{2-1}=2$ and slope of $BC=\dfrac{8-4}{4-2}=2$; equal slopes through a common point mean the three points are collinear, forming a straight line.

questions.q: If lines represented by $x+3y-6=0$, $2x+y-4=0$ and $kx-3y+1=0$ are concurrent, then the value of $k$ is ............
questions.explanation: Solving the first two lines gives the intersection $\left(\dfrac{6}{5},\dfrac{8}{5}\right)$. Substituting into $kx-3y+1=0$ gives $6k-19=0$, so $k=\dfrac{19}{6}$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{a+2x}-\sqrt{3x}}{\sqrt{3a+x}-2\sqrt{x}}\right]=.................$
questions.explanation: Both numerator and denominator vanish at $x=a$; applying L'Hopital's rule, $f'(a)=\dfrac{-1}{2\sqrt{3a}}$ and $g'(a)=\dfrac{-3}{4\sqrt a}$, giving the limit $\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt3}$. (KEA awarded a grace mark for this question; answer as per calculation.)

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\log x}{x-1} & \text{if }x\neq1\\ k & \text{if }x=1\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=1$, then the value of $k$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\dfrac{\log x}{x-1}=1$ (a standard limit), so for continuity $k=1$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\-\sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$, then $A\cdot A'$ is ............
questions.explanation: Multiplying $A$ by its transpose gives $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$ on the diagonal and $0$ off it, i.e. $A\cdot A'=I$.

questions.q: If $\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & -1\\1 & x-2 & 1\\x & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$ is singular, then the value of $x$ is ............
questions.explanation: Expanding the determinant gives $x^2+x-6=0$, i.e. $(x+3)(x-2)=0$, so $x=2$ (among the given options).

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of the same order, then which one of the following is NOT true?
questions.explanation: $(AB-BA)'=B'A'-A'B'=BA-AB=-(AB-BA)$, so $AB-BA$ is skew-symmetric, not symmetric in general.

questions.q: If $\omega$ is an imaginary cube root of unity, then the value of $\begin{vmatrix}1 & \omega^2 & 1-\omega^4\\omega & 1 & 1+\omega^5\\1 & \omega & \omega^2\end{vmatrix}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Using $\omega^3=1$ and $1+\omega+\omega^2=0$ to simplify entries ($\omega^4=\omega$, $\omega^5=\omega^2$) and expanding the determinant gives $\omega^2-4$.

questions.q: If $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\vec c$ are unit vectors such that $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$ then angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ is ...........
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=0$ gives $3+2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)=0$. By symmetry each dot product is $-\dfrac12$, so $\cos\theta=-\dfrac12$, i.e. $\theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.q: If $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\vec c$ are noncoplanar, then the value of $\vec a\cdot\left\{\dfrac{\vec b\times\vec c}{3\vec b\cdot(\vec c\times\vec a)}\right\}-\vec b\cdot\left\{\dfrac{\vec c\times\vec a}{2\vec c\cdot(\vec a\times\vec b)}\right\}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Since $\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b\cdot(\vec c\times\vec a)=\vec c\cdot(\vec a\times\vec b)=[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]=V$, the expression equals $\dfrac{V}{3V}-\dfrac{V}{2V}=\dfrac13-\dfrac12=-\dfrac16$.

questions.q: If $2\hat i+3\hat j$, $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and $\lambda\hat i+4\hat j+2\hat k$ taken in an order are coterminous edges of a parallelopiped of volume 2 Cu units, then value of $\lambda$ is ............
questions.explanation: The scalar triple product $\begin{vmatrix}2&3&0\\1&1&1\\lambda&4&2\end{vmatrix}=3\lambda-10$. Setting $|3\lambda-10|=2$ gives $\lambda=4$ or $\lambda=8/3$; among the options $\lambda=4$.

questions.q: A unit vector perpendicular to both $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and $2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$ is ............
questions.explanation: $(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\times(2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k)=2\hat i-\hat j-\hat k$, which has magnitude $\sqrt6$; dividing by this gives the unit vector.

questions.q: The digit in the unit's place of $7^{171}+(177)!$ is ............
questions.explanation: $177!$ ends in $0$. Units digits of $7^n$ cycle as $7,9,3,1$; since $171=4\times42+3$, $7^{171}$ ends in the 3rd term of the cycle, $3$. So the total unit's digit is $3+0=3$.

questions.q: The sum of all positive divisors of 242 except 1 and itself is ............
On the set of all nonzero reals, an operation $*$ is defined as $a*b=\dfrac{3ab}{2}$. In this group, a solution of $(2*x)*3^{-1}=4^{-1}$ is ............
questions.explanation: $2*x=3x$, then $(3x)*3^{-1}=\dfrac32x$. Setting $\dfrac32x=\dfrac14$ gives $x=\dfrac16$.

questions.q: $G=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}x & x\\x & x\end{bmatrix}, x\text{ is a nonzero real number}\right\}$ is a group with respect to matrix multiplication. In this group, the inverse of $\begin{bmatrix}1/3 & 1/3\\1/3 & 1/3\end{bmatrix}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Multiplying two such matrices with entries $x$ and $y$ gives entries $2xy$, so the identity element has $e=\dfrac12$. For $x=\dfrac13$, the inverse $y$ satisfies $2\cdot\dfrac13\cdot y=\dfrac12$, giving $y=\dfrac34$.

questions.q: If $2x^2+2y^2+4x+5y+1=0$ and $3x^2+3y^2+6x-7y+3k=0$ are orthogonal, then value of $k$ is ............
questions.explanation: Dividing to standard form: $g_1=1,f_1=1.25,c_1=0.5$ and $g_2=1,f_2=-7/6,c_2=k$. Orthogonality $2g_1g_2+2f_1f_2=c_1+c_2$ gives $k=\dfrac{-17}{12}$.

questions.q: The total number of common tangents of $x^2+y^2-6x-8y+9=0$ and $x^2+y^2=1$ is ............
questions.explanation: The first circle has centre $(3,4)$, radius $4$; the second has centre $(0,0)$, radius $1$. Distance between centres $=5=4+1$, so the circles touch externally, giving $3$ common tangents.

questions.q: The center of a circle which cuts $x^2+y^2+6x-1=0$, $x^2+y^2-3y+2=0$ and $x^2+y^2+x+y-3=0$ orthogonally is ............
questions.explanation: Setting up the three orthogonality conditions $2gg_i+2ff_i=c+c_i$ and solving simultaneously gives $g=1/7$, $f=-9/7$, so the centre $(-g,-f)=\left(\dfrac{-1}{7},\dfrac97\right)$.

questions.q: The length of the latus rectum of $3x^2-4y+6x-3=0$ is ............
questions.explanation: Rewriting as $(x+1)^2=\dfrac43\left(y+\dfrac32\right)$, we get $4p=\dfrac43$, which is the length of the latus rectum.

questions.q: The sum of the reciprocals of focal distances of a focal chord $PQ$ of $y^2=4ax$ is ............
questions.explanation: For a focal chord of $y^2=4ax$, the standard result is that the sum of the reciprocals of the segments' lengths from the focus equals $\dfrac1a$.

questions.q: If the focii of $\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$ and $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{3}=1$ coincide, then value of $a$ is ............
questions.explanation: For the ellipse, $c^2=16-4=12$. For the hyperbola, $c^2=a^2+3$. Equating gives $a^2=9$, i.e. $a=3$, which does not match any given option (likely a printing error in the paper); KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The equation of a hyperbola whose asymptotes are $3x\pm5y=0$ and vertices are $(\pm5,0)$ is ............
questions.explanation: With $a=5$ and asymptote slope $b/a=3/5$ giving $b=3$, the hyperbola is $\dfrac{x^2}{25}-\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$, i.e. $9x^2-25y^2=225$.

questions.q: The domain of $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left[\log_2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]$ is ............
questions.explanation: We need $-1\leq\log_2(x/2)\leq1$, i.e. $\dfrac12\leq\dfrac x2\leq2$, giving $1\leq x\leq4$.

questions.q: If $\tan^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac13\right)$, then $x$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4-\tan^{-1}\dfrac13\right)=\dfrac{1-1/3}{1+1/3}=\dfrac12$, so $x=\dfrac12$.

questions.q: A value of $\theta$ satisfying $\sin5\theta-\sin3\theta+\sin\theta=0$ such that $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\sin5\theta+\sin\theta=2\sin3\theta\cos2\theta$, so the equation becomes $\sin3\theta(2\cos2\theta-1)=0$. Taking $\cos2\theta=\dfrac12$ gives $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, which lies in the given range.

questions.q: The value of $\left|\dfrac{1+i\sqrt3}{\left(1+\dfrac{1}{i+1}\right)^2}\right|$ is ............
questions.explanation: $1+\dfrac{1}{i+1}=\dfrac{3-i}{2}$, whose square is $\dfrac{4-3i}{2}$. Then $\left|\dfrac{1+i\sqrt3}{(4-3i)/2}\right|=\dfrac{2\times2}{5}=\dfrac45$.

questions.q: If $\omega$ is an imaginary cube root of unity, then the value of $(1-\omega+\omega^2)\cdot(1-\omega^2+\omega^4)\cdot(1-\omega^4+\omega^8)\cdot...........(2n\text{ factors})$ is ............
questions.explanation: Each pair of factors simplifies to $(-2\omega)(-2\omega^2)=4\omega^3=4$; with $n$ such pairs among $2n$ factors, the product is $4^n=2^{2n}$.

questions.q: If $P(x,y)$ denotes $z=x+iy$ in Argand's plane and $\left|\dfrac{z-1}{z+2i}\right|=1$, then the locus of $P$ is a/an .........................
questions.explanation: $|z-1|=|z+2i|$ means $P$ is equidistant from $(1,0)$ and $(0,-2)$, so the locus is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them, a straight line.

questions.q: If $\sqrt r=ae^{\theta\cot\alpha}$ where $a$ and $\alpha$ are real numbers, then $\dfrac{d^2r}{d\theta^2}-4r\cot^2\alpha$ is ............
questions.explanation: $r=a^2e^{2\theta\cot\alpha}$, so $\dfrac{dr}{d\theta}=2\cot\alpha\cdot r$ and $\dfrac{d^2r}{d\theta^2}=4\cot^2\alpha\cdot r$; hence the expression is $0$.

questions.q: The derivative of $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right]$ with respect to $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right]$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right]=\dfrac x2$ and $\tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right]=\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac x2$. The derivative of the first with respect to the second is $\dfrac{1/2}{-1/2}=-1$.

questions.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\cos^2\left(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}}\right)\right]$ is ............
questions.explanation: With $\cot\theta=\sqrt{\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}}$, $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{\cot^2\theta}{1+\cot^2\theta}=\dfrac{2+x}{4}$, whose derivative with respect to $x$ is $\dfrac14$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin^2x}{1+\cot x}+\dfrac{\cos^2x}{1+\tan x}$, then $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is ............
questions.explanation: Simplifying, $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin^3x+\cos^3x}{\sin x+\cos x}=1-\sin x\cos x=1-\dfrac12\sin2x$, so $f'(x)=-\cos2x$, and $f'(\pi/4)=-\cos(\pi/2)=0$.

questions.q: If $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac yb\right)=n\log\left(\dfrac xn\right)$, then .......................
questions.explanation: Differentiating, $\dfrac{-y_1}{\sqrt{b^2-y^2}}=\dfrac nx$, so $xy_1+n\sqrt{b^2-y^2}=0$.

questions.q: Area of a triangle formed by tangent and normal to the curve $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ at $P\left(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt2},\dfrac{b}{\sqrt2}\right)$ with the $X$-axis is ........
questions.explanation: The tangent meets the $X$-axis at $(a\sqrt2,0)$ and the normal meets it at $\left(\dfrac{a^2-b^2}{a\sqrt2},0\right)$; with the height $b/\sqrt2$ from $P$, the triangle's area works out to $\dfrac{b(a^2+b^2)}{4a}$.

questions.q: The angle between $y^2=4x$ and $x^2+y^2=12$ at a point of their intersection is ............
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $(2,2\sqrt2)$, where the slopes are $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$; the angle between them is $\tan^{-1}(2\sqrt2)$.

questions.q: A sphere increases its volume at the rate of $\pi$ cc/s. The rate at which its surface area increases when the radius is 1 cm is ............
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\pi$ gives $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{4r^2}$. Then $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=8\pi r\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{2\pi}{r}$, which at $r=1$ is $2\pi$ sq.cm/s.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int_0^4|x-1|\,dx$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x)dx+\int_1^4(x-1)dx=\dfrac12+\dfrac92=5$.

questions.q: If $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^nx\,dx$, where $n$ is a positive integer, then $I_{10}+I_8$ is ............
questions.explanation: Using $I_n+I_{n-2}=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^{n-2}x\sec^2x\,dx=\dfrac{1}{n-1}$ with $n=10$ gives $I_{10}+I_8=\dfrac19$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int e^x\left[\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{1-\sin^2x}\right]dx$ is ............
questions.explanation: The integrand simplifies to $e^x[\sec x\tan x+\sec x]$, which is of the form $e^x[f(x)+f'(x)]$ with $f(x)=\sec x$, so the integral is $e^x\sec x+c$.

questions.q: When $x>0$, then $\displaystyle\int\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)dx$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$, so the integral is $2\displaystyle\int\tan^{-1}x\,dx=2x\tan^{-1}x-\log(1+x^2)+c$.

questions.q: If the area between $y=mx^2$ and $x=my^2$ ($m>0$) is $\dfrac14$ sq. units, then value of $m$ is ............
questions.explanation: The area between the curves is $\displaystyle\int_0^{1/m}\left[\sqrt{x/m}-mx^2\right]dx=\dfrac{1}{3m^2}$. Setting this to $\dfrac14$ gives $m=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$, which does not exactly match any given option; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: If $m$ and $n$ are degree and order of $\left(1+y_1^2\right)^{2/3}=y_2$, then the value of $\dfrac{m+n}{m-n}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Cubing both sides gives $(1+y_1^2)^2=y_2^3$, a polynomial equation with order $n=2$ (highest derivative $y_2$) and degree $m=3$. So $\dfrac{m+n}{m-n}=\dfrac{5}{1}=5$.

questions.q: The general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1-x^2-y^2+x^2y^2$ is ............
questions.explanation: The right side factors as $(1-x^2)(1-y^2)$. Taking this to mean $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}$ (the intended equation, since the printed form without a square root does not lead to any listed answer), separating variables gives $\sin^{-1}y=\dfrac x2\sqrt{1-x^2}+\dfrac12\sin^{-1}x+C$, i.e. $2\sin^{-1}y=x\sqrt{1-x^2}+\sin^{-1}x+c$. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: If $x\cos\alpha+y\sin\alpha=4$ is tangent to $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$, then the value of $\alpha$ is ............
questions.explanation: Tangency requires $16=25\cos^2\alpha+9\sin^2\alpha=9+16\cos^2\alpha$, giving $\cos^2\alpha=7/16$ and $\tan\alpha=3/\sqrt7$.

questions.q: If $P$ is a point on $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ with focii $S$ and $S'$, then the maximum value of triangle $SPS'$ is ............
questions.explanation: The base $SS'=2ae$ is fixed, and the height is maximised at $b$ (the end of the minor axis), giving maximum area $\dfrac12\times2ae\times b=abe$.

questions.q: In Argand's plane, the point corresponding to $\dfrac{(1-i\sqrt3)(1+i)}{(\sqrt3+i)}$ lies in ............
questions.explanation: Simplifying the expression gives $1-i$, which corresponds to the point $(1,-1)$, lying in quadrant IV.

questions.q: If $y=\sin x\cdot\sin2x\cdot\sin3x...........\sin nx$, then $y'$ is ............
questions.explanation: Taking logarithms, $\ln y=\sum\ln(\sin kx)$, so $\dfrac{y'}{y}=\sum k\cot kx$, i.e. $y'=y\cdot\sum_{k=1}^n k\cot kx$.

questions.q: $\begin{vmatrix}\sin\alpha & \cos\alpha & \sin(\alpha+\delta)\\sin\beta & \cos\beta & \sin(\beta+\delta)\\sin\gamma & \cos\gamma & \sin(\gamma+\delta)\end{vmatrix}=.............................$
questions.explanation: Since $\sin(\theta+\delta)=\cos\delta\sin\theta+\sin\delta\cos\theta$, the third column is a linear combination of the first two columns, making the determinant $0$.
